meta.title: Star Wars D6 Rules Reference
meta.system: Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (West End Games, 2nd Edition Revised & Expanded)
meta.notes: Keyword-search knowledge base. Add more chunks to expand coverage. Future: add vector embeddings for RAG.

chunks.title: Core Mechanic & Dice Codes
chunks.text: Star Wars D6 uses six-sided dice (D6) exclusively. Characters have attributes and skills rated in 'dice codes' like 3D, 4D+1, or 5D+2. The number before the D is how many dice you roll; the +1 or +2 (called 'pips') is added to the total after rolling. For example, 3D+2 means roll 3 six-sided dice, add them together, then add 2. To attempt an action, the GM sets a difficulty number. The player rolls the dice for the relevant skill (or attribute if they lack the skill) and tries to meet or exceed the difficulty. If you equal or beat it, you succeed. The higher you roll above the difficulty, the better you succeed. Rolling under means failure, and the further under, the worse the failure. Dice codes advance in pips: 3D → 3D+1 → 3D+2 → 4D. Three pips equal one full die. This is the fundamental mechanic for everything in the game — combat, skills, Force powers, vehicle operations, and social encounters.

chunks.title: The Wild Die
chunks.text: One die in every roll is designated the Wild Die (usually a different color). The Wild Die adds excitement and unpredictability. If you roll a 6 on the Wild Die, add 6 to your total and roll it again — keep adding and rerolling as long as you keep rolling 6s. This means any roll has the potential for spectacular success. If you roll a 1 on the Wild Die on the initial roll, the GM may introduce a complication or 'twist of fate.' In some versions, a 1 means you remove the Wild Die AND the highest other die from your total. The complication should be dramatic but not necessarily devastating — a blaster might overheat, you might slip, or attract unwanted attention. The Wild Die makes every roll exciting because even a character with low dice can sometimes pull off amazing feats, and skilled characters can still have things go wrong in interesting ways.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: Characters have six attributes that define their basic capabilities. DEXTERITY governs hand-eye coordination, agility, and reflexes — shooting blasters, dodging, melee combat, throwing, and piloting ground vehicles. KNOWLEDGE represents education, common sense, and willpower — knowing alien species, bureaucratic procedures, languages, planetary systems, streetwise, survival, and resisting mental influence. MECHANICAL covers the operation of vehicles, starships, and mechanical systems — astrogation, piloting starfighters and space transports, operating shields and sensors, and riding beasts. PERCEPTION measures awareness, charisma, and social skills — bargaining, commanding, conning, gambling, hiding, investigating, persuading, searching, and sneaking. STRENGTH represents physical power and toughness — brawling, climbing, jumping, lifting, stamina, and swimming. It is also rolled to resist damage. TECHNICAL covers repair, programming, and technical knowledge — fixing droids and starships, computer programming, demolitions, first aid, medicine, and security systems. Humans allocate 18D among attributes with a minimum of 2D and maximum of 4D in each. Alien species have different ranges.

chunks.title: Skills
chunks.text: Skills represent trained abilities that fall under one of the six attributes. If a character doesn't have a specific skill, they roll the base attribute instead. Skills start at the attribute's dice code and can be improved with skill dice during character creation or Character Points during play. At character creation, players have 7D to distribute among skills. Each die placed in a skill adds to the attribute's base. For example, if Dexterity is 3D and you put 1D in Blaster, your Blaster skill is 4D. Key skills by attribute: DEXTERITY: Blaster, Bowcaster, Brawling Parry, Dodge, Grenade, Lightsaber, Melee Combat, Melee Parry, Missile Weapons, Thrown Weapons, Vehicle Blasters. KNOWLEDGE: Alien Species, Bureaucracy, Cultures, Languages, Law Enforcement, Planetary Systems, Streetwise, Survival, Tactics, Willpower. MECHANICAL: Astrogation, Beast Riding, Communications, Repulsorlift Operation, Sensors, Space Transports, Starfighter Piloting, Starship Gunnery, Starship Shields, Swoop Operation. PERCEPTION: Bargain, Command, Con, Forgery, Gambling, Hide, Investigation, Persuasion, Search, Sneak. STRENGTH: Brawling, Climbing/Jumping, Lifting, Stamina, Swimming. TECHNICAL: Armor Repair, Blaster Repair, Computer Programming/Repair, Demolitions, Droid Programming, Droid Repair, First Aid, Medicine, Repulsorlift Repair, Security, Space Transport Repair, Starfighter Repair, Starship Weapon Repair. Specializations cost less to improve and apply to a narrower area (e.g., Blaster: Heavy Blaster Pistol).

chunks.title: Difficulty Numbers
chunks.text: The GM sets difficulty numbers for tasks based on how hard they are. Standard difficulties: VERY EASY (1-5): Almost anyone can do this. Routine tasks under normal conditions. EASY (6-10): Most characters can handle this. Requires some skill or effort. MODERATE (11-15): Requires a fair amount of skill. Average difficulty for trained characters. DIFFICULT (16-20): Only highly skilled characters regularly succeed. Challenging tasks. VERY DIFFICULT (21-25): Even experts find this hard. Extraordinary effort required. HEROIC (26-30): Nearly impossible. Only the most skilled, with luck, can pull this off. HEROIC+ (31+): The stuff of legends. Requires extreme skill AND the Force or other advantages. For OPPOSED ROLLS, both characters roll their relevant skill/attribute. The higher total wins. Ties go to the character who initiated the action (attacker in combat, persuader in social). The GM may also add modifiers: favorable conditions might lower difficulty, while adverse conditions raise it. Example modifiers: dim lighting +5 to difficulty, heavy rain +10, character is wounded -1D to skill.

chunks.title: Character Creation
chunks.text: To create a character: 1) Choose a template or build from scratch. Templates are pre-made archetypes (Smuggler, Bounty Hunter, Brash Pilot, etc.) with attributes already allocated and some skills filled in. 2) If building from scratch, allocate 18D among the six attributes (humans). Minimum 2D, maximum 4D per attribute. 3) Distribute 7D among skills. Each die adds to the attribute base. You can split dice into pips (+1, +2). No skill may be raised more than 2D above its base attribute at creation. 4) Choose equipment appropriate to your concept (GM approval). Starting credits vary by template, typically 1,000-2,000 credits. 5) Write a background — name, species, homeworld, history, personality, goals, and connections. 6) Starting Force-sensitive characters must declare it at creation. They get Force skills (Control, Sense, Alter) at 0D but can allocate skill dice into them. They also start with 1-2 Force Points and must choose initial Force powers. 7) All starting characters get 5 Character Points and 1 Force Point (2 if Force-sensitive). 8) The GM may allow or restrict certain templates or species based on the era and campaign setting.

chunks.title: Character Templates
chunks.text: Templates provide ready-made character concepts. Classic Star Wars D6 templates include: SMUGGLER — Fast-talking pilot with a ship and debts. High Mechanical and Perception. BOUNTY HUNTER — Ruthless tracker. High Dexterity and Perception. BRASH PILOT — Hotshot flyboy who lives for speed. High Mechanical and Dexterity. YOUNG JEDI — Force-sensitive youth discovering their powers. Balanced attributes with Force skills. FAILED JEDI — Trained but left the path. Has some Force ability and regrets. KID — Young and scrappy with surprising resourcefulness. High Perception. GAMBLER — Lives by luck and wits. High Perception, especially Gambling and Con. LACONIC SCOUT — Quiet explorer of the galaxy's frontier. High Mechanical and Knowledge (Survival, Planetary Systems). MERCENARY — Soldier of fortune. High Dexterity (Blaster) and Strength. MON CALAMARI — Aquatic species, often officers or technicians. QUIXOTIC JEDI — Idealistic Force user, possibly naive. OLD SENATORIAL — Experienced politician. High Knowledge and Perception social skills. OUTLAW — Criminal on the run. High Dexterity and Streetwise. RETIRED CAPTAIN — Former military officer with leadership skills. TONGUE-TIED ENGINEER — Brilliant technician, terrible communicator. High Technical. WOOKIEE — Powerful, loyal companion. Very high Strength. MINOR JEDI — Has some training but not a full Jedi Knight yet. Players may customize templates by shifting a few dice around with GM permission.

chunks.title: Species
chunks.text: Alien species have different attribute ranges than humans and often have special abilities. HUMANS: 2D-4D in all attributes, 18D total. The most common species. WOOKIEES: Higher Strength (3D-6D), lower Knowledge and Technical ranges. Special: Berserker Rage (+2D to Strength in combat when enraged), Climbing Claws. Cannot speak Basic. TWI'LEKS: Similar to human ranges. Head-tails (lekku) used in secret communication. Many are diplomats or dancers. RODIANS: Slightly higher Dexterity. Natural hunters with keen senses. MON CALAMARI: Slightly higher Knowledge and Technical. Can breathe underwater, swim at normal speed. Often military leaders or artists. BOTHANS: Higher Perception. Natural spies and information brokers. SULLUSTANS: Higher Mechanical. Expert navigators, can navigate underground by sense. ITHORIANS: Higher Knowledge. 'Hammerheads.' Can produce a devastating bellow sonic attack. Peaceful herbivores who worship nature. GAMORREANS: Much higher Strength (3D-5D), lower Knowledge and Technical. Porcine warriors who rely on brute force. TRANDOSHANS: Higher Strength and Dexterity. Natural hunters, claws (+1D damage in brawling), can regenerate lost limbs slowly. Rivals of Wookiees. CEREANS: Higher Knowledge. Binary brains allow enhanced thinking. ZABRAK: Higher Willpower. Horned heads, determined and tenacious. When creating an alien character, use that species' attribute minimums and maximums, and their total attribute dice (may differ from 18D).

chunks.title: Character Points
chunks.text: Character Points (CP) represent a character's ability to push beyond normal limits through determination and minor Force attunement. SPENDING CP: Before or after any roll, a player may spend Character Points. Each CP spent lets you roll one additional die and add it to your total. You can spend multiple CP on a single roll. The Wild Die rules do NOT apply to Character Point dice. Spent CP are gone permanently (until you earn more). EARNING CP: The GM awards CP at the end of each session, typically 3-15 points based on: completing objectives, good roleplaying, clever solutions, advancing the story, heroic actions. A routine session might award 3-5 CP; a dramatic, story-significant session might award 8-15. SAVING CP: CP are also the currency for permanent character advancement (improving skills and attributes between adventures). Players must balance spending CP for immediate success versus saving them for long-term growth. There is no maximum to how many CP a character can hold. A character CANNOT spend Character Points in the same round they spend a Force Point.

chunks.title: Force Points
chunks.text: Force Points represent dramatic, heroic effort — the galaxy's destiny nudging events. They are much more powerful but rarer than Character Points. SPENDING A FORCE POINT: When you spend a Force Point, ALL your skill and attribute die codes are DOUBLED for the rest of that round. A character with Blaster 5D would roll 10D. This is incredibly powerful and represents a moment of supreme effort. You may only spend ONE Force Point per round. You cannot spend Character Points in the same round you use a Force Point. EARNING FORCE POINTS: If you spend a Force Point heroically at a dramatically appropriate moment (like Luke's trench run shot), you get it back and gain one additional Force Point. If you spend one at a non-dramatic moment, you simply lose it. If you use a Force Point for evil, selfish, or aggressive purposes, you don't get it back AND you gain a Dark Side Point. STARTING FORCE POINTS: Characters typically start with 1 Force Point (2 if Force-sensitive). Force Points are the rarest and most powerful resource in the game — save them for the moments that truly matter.

chunks.title: Dark Side Points
chunks.text: The Dark Side of the Force tempts those who use power for selfish or aggressive ends. GAINING DARK SIDE POINTS: A character gains a Dark Side Point when they: use the Force to cause harm motivated by anger, hatred, or aggression; use a Force Point for evil or selfish purposes; perform acts of needless cruelty or murder; torture, betray allies, or commit atrocities. The GM decides when an action warrants a DSP, but the key test is motivation — killing in genuine self-defense usually doesn't earn one; killing out of anger or revenge does. CALLING UPON THE DARK SIDE: A Force-sensitive character may 'call upon the Dark Side' for extra power. The character rolls their number of Dark Side Points as extra dice added to any Force skill roll. However, they must then make a Willpower check — if they fail, they gain another Dark Side Point. FALLING TO THE DARK SIDE: When a character accumulates 6 or more Dark Side Points, they have fallen to the Dark Side and become an NPC villain under the GM's control (or may be redeemed through a long quest). ATONEMENT: A character can work off Dark Side Points through genuinely selfless, heroic acts. The GM may remove 1 DSP after an extended period of righteous behavior. Redemption is possible but difficult — this mirrors the Star Wars themes of temptation and redemption.

chunks.title: Combat Rounds & Actions
chunks.text: Combat is organized into rounds, each representing about 5 seconds of game time. ROUND STRUCTURE: 1) All players and NPCs declare their intended actions. 2) The GM determines the order of actions (usually highest Perception goes first, or narratively appropriate). 3) Actions are resolved. MULTIPLE ACTIONS: A character can attempt more than one action per round, but suffers a cumulative penalty: -1D for each action beyond the first. Two actions = -1D to both. Three actions = -2D to all three. Four actions = -3D to all four. And so on. This represents dividing attention. REACTIONS: Dodging and parrying are 'reaction skills' that can be used without counting as an action, BUT only at the base skill level (no bonuses). To get full dice, you must declare a dodge/parry as one of your actions. FULL DODGE/PARRY: If you dedicate your entire round to dodging, you add your full dodge skill to the difficulty of all attacks against you that round. Full parry works similarly for melee. FREE ACTIONS: Speaking a short sentence, dropping an item, or looking around are free and don't count as actions. MOVEMENT: Moving a short distance (walking/jogging) is free. Running requires an action. All-out sprinting is a full action.

chunks.title: Combat - Attacking & Defending
chunks.text: RANGED COMBAT: The attacker rolls their weapon skill (usually Blaster). The difficulty is based on range: Point Blank (0-2m) = Easy (6-10) with a +5 bonus to hit (so effectively very easy); Short Range = Easy (10); Medium Range = Moderate (15); Long Range = Difficult (20). If the target uses a Dodge reaction, the dodge roll replaces the range difficulty if it's higher. Cover modifiers increase difficulty: light cover +1D to difficulty, half cover +2D, heavy cover +4D. MELEE COMBAT: The attacker rolls Melee Combat or Brawling. The difficulty is the defender's Melee Parry, Brawling Parry, or Dodge roll (whichever they use). Melee is always an opposed roll. CALLED SHOTS: Targeting a specific body part or small area increases difficulty by +1D to +3D depending on size. DRAWING A WEAPON: Drawing or holstering a weapon counts as an action (applies multiple action penalty). Characters who keep weapons ready avoid this. SURPRISE: If a target is surprised, they cannot dodge or parry. The attacker rolls against base difficulty only.

chunks.title: Damage & Wound Levels
chunks.text: When an attack hits, damage is determined by comparing the attack's damage roll against the target's Strength roll (plus armor). DAMAGE RESOLUTION: The attacker rolls the weapon's damage dice. The defender rolls Strength (plus any armor bonus). Compare the totals: Damage ≤ Strength = No damage. Damage exceeds Strength by 1-3 = STUNNED: -1D to all actions for the rest of the round. Multiple stuns become a wound. Damage exceeds Strength by 4-8 = WOUNDED: -1D penalty to all actions until healed. Character falls prone. Damage exceeds Strength by 9-12 = INCAPACITATED: Character collapses, unconscious. Cannot take actions. Will die without medical attention if mortally wounded next. Damage exceeds Strength by 13-15 = MORTALLY WOUNDED: Character is dying. Will die without immediate medical attention (within ~5 rounds). Damage exceeds Strength by 16+ = KILLED: Character is dead. WOUND STACKING: A character who is already Wounded and gets Wounded again becomes Wounded Twice (-2D to all actions). A Wounded Twice character who takes another wound becomes Incapacitated. STUN DAMAGE: Some weapons deal stun damage (set to stun). Stun wounds heal faster and cannot kill, but enough stun damage can knock someone unconscious.

chunks.title: Healing
chunks.text: Healing in Star Wars D6 uses First Aid, Medicine, and natural recovery. FIRST AID: Can be used immediately after injury. Difficulty varies: Stunned = Very Easy (5), Wounded = Easy (10), Incapacitated = Moderate (15), Mortally Wounded = Difficult (20). Success heals one wound level. Can only be attempted once per injury. Using a medpac gives +1D to the First Aid roll. MEDICINE: For more serious treatment. Requires medical supplies or a medical facility. Can heal beyond what First Aid accomplishes. Difficulty: Wounded = Moderate (15), Incapacitated = Difficult (20), Mortally Wounded = Very Difficult (25). Bacta tanks provide a +2D bonus and heal rapidly. NATURAL HEALING: Without treatment, characters heal naturally but slowly. A Wounded character heals in 3 days with bed rest (Strength roll, Moderate difficulty). Incapacitated characters need 2 weeks. Mortally Wounded characters cannot heal naturally without being stabilized first. MEDPACS: Standard medpac provides +1D to First Aid rolls. Each medpac is single-use. BACTA TANK: Full bacta immersion heals all wound levels in 1-5 days depending on severity. Requires proper medical facility.

chunks.title: The Force - Overview
chunks.text: The Force is an energy field generated by all living things that binds the galaxy together. In game terms, the Force is governed by three Force skills: CONTROL: Power over your own body and mind. Self-healing, pain resistance, enhancing attributes, meditation. SENSE: Awareness of the Force and the living world. Detecting life, danger sense, reading emotions, telepathy. ALTER: Using the Force to affect the physical world. Telekinesis, harming others, affecting minds. To use Force powers, a character must be Force-sensitive (declared at creation) and have at least some training in the relevant Force skill(s). Using the Force is not without risk — using it aggressively or selfishly earns Dark Side Points. Each Force power requires specific Force skill rolls, and many require combinations (Control + Sense, Sense + Alter, Control + Sense + Alter). Force powers have their own difficulty numbers. Maintaining a Force power across multiple rounds costs a multi-action penalty. Jedi characters must balance power with responsibility — the Dark Side is always tempting.

chunks.title: Force Powers - Control
chunks.text: Control powers affect the Force user's own body and mind. Key Control powers: ACCELERATE HEALING (Control, Moderate): Enter a trance to heal faster. Heals one wound level per day of meditation. CONCENTRATION (Control, Easy-Difficult): Focus to resist distraction. Add Control dice to Willpower rolls. CONTROL PAIN (Control, Easy-Difficult depending on wound): Ignore wound penalties for a time. Doesn't actually heal, just suppresses pain. DETOXIFY POISON (Control, Easy-Very Difficult): Purge toxins from your own body. EMPTINESS/RAGE (Control, Moderate): Deep meditation that hides you from Force detection. Light side = Emptiness, Dark side = Rage. ENHANCE ATTRIBUTE (Control, Moderate): Temporarily boost one attribute. Add Control roll bonus to one attribute for one round. Very versatile. FORCE OF WILL (Control, Easy): Bolster your Willpower against mental attacks and Force powers. HIBERNATION TRANCE (Control, Difficult): Enter suspended animation, reducing life functions to near-death. Useful for surviving in vacuum, conserving air, or faking death. REDUCE INJURY (Control, Moderate-Difficult): Use immediately when damaged. Reduce wound severity by one level. REMAIN CONSCIOUS (Control, Easy-Difficult): Stay awake and acting even when wounded enough to pass out. RESIST STUN (Control, Moderate): Prepare your body to resist stun damage.

chunks.title: Force Powers - Sense
chunks.text: Sense powers let the Force user perceive the Force and living beings. Key Sense powers: COMBAT SENSE (Sense, Moderate): In combat, add Sense dice to all dodge and parry rolls for one round. Essentially 'feeling' attacks before they arrive. DANGER SENSE (Sense, Moderate-Heroic): Sense immediate threats. Provides a warning before an ambush, trap, or attack. The more dangerous the threat, the harder the roll. LIFE DETECTION (Sense, Very Easy-Moderate): Detect living beings within range. Can sense general emotions and intent. Range and detail depend on success level. LIFE SENSE (Sense, Easy-Difficult): More detailed version of Life Detection. Can identify specific individuals, determine health and emotional state. MAGNIFY SENSES (Sense, Very Easy-Moderate): Enhance your natural senses. See farther, hear better, detect faint smells. RECEPTIVE TELEPATHY (Sense, Very Easy-Heroic): Read surface thoughts of a willing target (Very Easy) or unwilling target (opposed by Willpower). Can read deeper thoughts at higher difficulties. SENSE FORCE (Sense, Moderate-Heroic): Detect the use of the Force nearby. Can sense Force-sensitive individuals, active Force powers, Dark Side locations, and powerful artifacts. TRANSLATION (Sense, Moderate): Understand unfamiliar spoken or written languages through the Force. WEATHER SENSE (Sense, Easy): Predict weather patterns through Force attunement.

chunks.title: Force Powers - Alter & Combined Powers
chunks.text: Alter powers affect the physical world. TELEKINESIS (Alter, Very Easy-Heroic): Move objects with the Force. Difficulty based on weight: 1kg = Very Easy, 10kg = Easy, 100kg = Moderate, 1000kg = Difficult, 10000kg = Very Difficult. Attacking with telekinesis earns a Dark Side Point unless in defense. INJURE/KILL (Alter, opposed by Willpower/Control): Cause pain or death. Always earns a Dark Side Point. COMBINED POWERS (require multiple Force skills): LIGHTSABER COMBAT (Control + Sense): Add Sense to lightsaber attack, Control to lightsaber damage. Essential for Jedi. PROJECTIVE TELEPATHY (Control + Sense): Send thoughts to others. ACCELERATE ANOTHER'S HEALING (Control + Alter): Heal others like Accelerate Healing but on another person. AFFECT MIND (Control + Sense + Alter): Alter a target's perceptions or plant suggestions. 'These aren't the droids you're looking for.' Higher difficulty for stronger effects. BATTLE MEDITATION (Control + Sense + Alter, Heroic): Coordinate and inspire allied forces in large-scale combat. Extremely powerful, very high difficulty. TELEKINETIC KILL (Control + Sense + Alter): Force choke. Always earns a Dark Side Point. FORCE HARMONY (Control + Sense + Alter): Multiple Jedi pool their Force abilities for greater effect.

chunks.title: Lightsaber Combat
chunks.text: Lightsaber Combat is a combined Control + Sense Force power that is essential for any Jedi. ACTIVATION: At the start of a round, the Jedi makes a Control roll and a Sense roll (counts as an action, incurring multi-action penalty if doing other things). If successful, the Jedi adds Sense dice to lightsaber attack rolls and Control dice to lightsaber damage rolls for that round. PARRYING BLASTER BOLTS: A Jedi can parry (block) incoming blaster bolts as a reaction. The difficulty is the attacker's roll. Success means the bolt is blocked harmlessly. DEFLECTING BOLTS BACK: The Jedi can attempt to redirect a blocked bolt back at the attacker or another target. This increases the difficulty and requires an additional action. The Jedi rolls Lightsaber skill to hit the new target. LIGHTSABER VS LIGHTSABER: When two lightsaber wielders duel, it becomes opposed Lightsaber rolls (both enhanced by their respective Lightsaber Combat powers). DAMAGE: A lightsaber deals 5D base damage, plus the user's Control dice from Lightsaber Combat. Lightsabers can cut through most materials. Against another lightsaber, the defender uses their lightsaber roll as a parry. LIMITATIONS: Lightsaber Combat must be activated each round. If the Jedi is injured or loses concentration, they may need to re-activate. Using Lightsaber Combat to strike down a helpless or surrendered opponent earns a Dark Side Point.

chunks.title: Equipment & Weapons
chunks.text: Standard weapons and gear in the Star Wars galaxy: BLASTERS: Hold-out Blaster (3D, concealable, 3-4/8/12m range), Blaster Pistol (4D, standard sidearm, 3-10/30/120m), Heavy Blaster Pistol (5D, powerful, 3-7/25/50m), Sporting Blaster (3D+1, civilian), Blaster Rifle (5D, military, 3-30/100/300m), Bowcaster (4D, Wookiee weapon, 3-10/30/50m). MELEE: Vibroblade (STR+2D), Vibro-ax (STR+3D), Force Pike (STR+2D, stun capable), Lightsaber (5D). HEAVY: Thermal Detonator (10D, 0-2/8/12/20m, devastating), Blaster Cannon (4D speeder-scale). ARMOR: Blast Vest (+1D physical, +1 energy), Blast Helmet (+1D physical, +1 energy to head), Stormtrooper Armor (+2D physical, +1D energy, -1D Dexterity penalty), Mandalorian Armor (varies, often +3D), Bounty Hunter Armor (varies). GEAR: Comlink (standard communication), Macrobinoculars (+3D to search at distance), Electrobinoculars (add low-light), Medpac (+1D to First Aid), Glow Rod (flashlight), Breath Mask (30 min air), Datapad (portable computer), Toolkit (required for repairs), Syntherope (20m), Ration Packs. COSTS: Blaster pistol ~500 credits, Heavy blaster ~750, Blaster rifle ~1,000, Stormtrooper armor ~Military only, Medpac ~100, Comlink ~25.

chunks.title: Vehicles
chunks.text: Vehicles in Star Wars D6 use the Speeder or Walker scale. Key vehicle stats: BODY: Structural integrity (like Strength for vehicles). MANEUVERABILITY: Bonus dice added to pilot rolls. SPEED: Maximum movement rate. WEAPONS: Damage rating at appropriate scale. VEHICLE TYPES: Landspeeder (X-34): Body 2D, Maneuverability 1D, Move 210/600 kmh. Civilian transport. Speeder Bike (74-Z): Body 1D+2, Maneuverability 3D+1, Move 500/1500 kmh. Fast and agile. AT-AT (Imperial Walker): Body 6D, Walker scale, Move 60/180 kmh, 2 heavy laser cannons (6D), 2 medium blasters (3D). AT-ST (Scout Walker): Body 3D, Walker scale, Move 90/270 kmh, twin blaster cannons (4D). T-47 Airspeeder (Snowspeeder): Body 2D, Maneuverability 2D, Atmospheric, twin laser cannon (4D+1), harpoon. Sail Barge: Body 3D+2, Heavy, deck-mounted laser cannon (3D). VEHICLE OPERATION: Pilot rolls Repulsorlift Operation or relevant vehicle skill. Difficulty depends on terrain and maneuvers. Stunts require higher difficulties. VEHICLE DAMAGE: Same wound track as characters but at vehicle scale: Lightly Damaged (controls -1D), Heavily Damaged (controls -2D), Severely Damaged (dead in water), Destroyed.

chunks.title: Starships
chunks.text: Starships operate at Starfighter or Capital scale. Key ship stats: HULL: Structural strength. SHIELDS: Add to damage resistance. MANEUVERABILITY: Bonus to piloting. HYPERDRIVE: Multiplier (x1 is fastest standard, x2 is slower, x0.5 is modified/faster). WEAPONS: Damage at starship scale. COMMON STARFIGHTERS: X-Wing (Hull 4D, Shields 1D, Maneuverability 3D, Hyperdrive x1, 4 Laser Cannons 6D, Proton Torpedoes 9D), Y-Wing (Hull 4D, Shields 1D+2, Maneuverability 1D, Hyperdrive x1, 2 Laser Cannons 5D, Proton Torpedoes 9D, Ion Cannon 4D), A-Wing (Hull 2D+2, Shields 1D, Maneuverability 4D, Hyperdrive x1, 2 Laser Cannons 5D), TIE Fighter (Hull 2D, No Shields, Maneuverability 2D, No Hyperdrive, 2 Laser Cannons 5D), TIE Interceptor (Hull 3D, No Shields, Maneuverability 3D+2, No Hyperdrive, 4 Laser Cannons 6D). FREIGHTERS: YT-1300 (Millennium Falcon type): Hull 4D, Shields 2D, Maneuverability 1D+2, Hyperdrive x0.5 (modified), Laser Cannons 4D+1 (2 quad turrets). CAPITAL SHIPS: Imperial Star Destroyer (Capital scale, Hull 7D, Shields 3D+1, 60 Turbolasers 4D capital, 60 Ion Cannons 3D capital, 10 Tractor Beams). Corellian Corvette (Capital scale, Hull 4D, Shields 2D, 6 Turbolasers 3D capital). SPACE COMBAT: Uses Space Transports, Starfighter Piloting, and Starship Gunnery skills.

chunks.title: Scale System
chunks.text: Different-sized combatants operate at different scales, which affects attacks between them. SCALES (smallest to largest): Character, Speeder, Walker, Starfighter, Capital. SCALE DIFFERENCES IN COMBAT: When a smaller-scale attacker fires at a larger-scale target, the attacker gets bonus dice to hit (the target is huge) but the damage is reduced against the larger target's resistance. When a larger-scale attacker fires at a smaller-scale target, the attacker suffers penalty dice to hit (the target is tiny and nimble) but the damage is devastating if it connects. SPECIFIC MODIFIERS: Each step of scale difference = approximately 6D modifier. Character vs Speeder: Character gets +6D to hit but the speeder resists with +6D. A speeder weapon hitting a character does +6D damage but has -6D to hit. Character vs Starfighter: +12D to hit / +12D resistance / -12D to hit from starfighter / +12D damage from starfighter. This is why a blaster pistol (4D) is essentially useless against a starfighter (which resists with Hull + 12D bonus), but a proton torpedo (9D starfighter scale, effectively 9D+12D = ~21D vs character scale) is instantly lethal to a person. PRACTICAL EFFECT: Stormtroopers can't shoot down X-wings with blaster rifles. Turbolasers can't reliably hit individual people. This scale system elegantly models the Star Wars feel where fighters and capital ships operate in different combat paradigms.

chunks.title: Astrogation & Hyperspace
chunks.text: Hyperspace travel is faster-than-light travel through an alternate dimension. ASTROGATION SKILL: Used to calculate hyperspace jumps. Difficulty depends on the route: Well-traveled route (Coruscant to Corellia) = Easy (10), Known but less common route = Moderate (15), Poorly charted route = Difficult (20), Unknown/hazardous route = Very Difficult to Heroic (25+). USING NAVIGATION COMPUTER: A ship's nav computer stores pre-calculated routes. Using a stored route is Very Easy (5). Calculating a new route yourself takes time: 1 minute for Easy, 10 minutes for Moderate, 30 minutes for Difficult, 1 hour+ for Very Difficult. MISHAPS: Failing an Astrogation roll by a small margin means a longer trip or dropping out of hyperspace early. Failing badly can mean flying through a star, a supernova, or an asteroid field — potentially destroying the ship. HYPERDRIVE MULTIPLIER: x1 is standard. x2 is half speed (most bulk freighters). x0.5 is twice as fast (rare, modified ships like the Falcon). Travel times are relative — a trip that takes 10 hours at x1 takes 20 hours at x2 or 5 hours at x0.5. HYPERSPACE LIMITATIONS: Hyperspace routes must avoid gravity wells (stars, planets, black holes). Interdictor cruisers generate artificial gravity wells to pull ships out of hyperspace. Ships cannot enter or exit hyperspace within a planet's gravity well (must reach orbit first).

chunks.title: Character Advancement
chunks.text: Characters improve between adventures by spending Character Points. IMPROVING SKILLS: To increase a skill by one pip (+1, +2, or to the next full die), the cost equals the current die code value in Character Points. For example, improving Blaster from 5D to 5D+1 costs 5 CP. From 5D+1 to 5D+2 costs 5 CP. From 5D+2 to 6D costs 5 CP. Training time: with a teacher, 1 day per CP spent. Without a teacher, 1 week per CP spent. IMPROVING ATTRIBUTES: Much harder. Cost = current die code x10 in Character Points. Improving Dexterity from 3D to 3D+1 costs 30 CP. Requires a teacher and extended training time (usually weeks to months). Attributes represent fundamental capabilities and improve slowly. LEARNING NEW SKILLS: Adding a new skill at the attribute level costs 0 — you already have it at the base attribute. Adding a specialization costs 1 CP for the first pip. FORCE POWERS: Learning a new Force power costs CP based on its difficulty: Very Easy = 1 CP, Easy = 3 CP, Moderate = 5 CP, Difficult = 10 CP, Very Difficult = 15 CP, Heroic = 20 CP. With a teacher, halve the time. Without a teacher, double the cost. FORCE SKILLS: Improve like regular skills but are more expensive without a master: without a teacher, costs are doubled.

chunks.title: Gamemaster Guidelines
chunks.text: Running Star Wars D6 emphasizes speed, excitement, and cinematic action. KEY PRINCIPLES: Keep it fast — if you can't find a rule in 30 seconds, make something up and keep going. The Rule of Fun trumps all: if a rule produces a boring result, ignore it. Star Wars is about drama, not simulation. SETTING DIFFICULTIES: Think about what would happen in the movies. If Han Solo would succeed at this casually, it's Easy. If he'd need to be at his best, it's Difficult. If only Luke channeling the Force could do it, it's Heroic. AWARDING CHARACTER POINTS: Base award 3-5 per session. Bonus +1-3 for good roleplaying, clever problem-solving, heroic sacrifice, or advancing personal story arcs. +1-2 for achieving mission objectives. AWARDING FORCE POINTS: A character who spent a Force Point heroically at a dramatically appropriate moment gets it back plus one. The 'dramatic moment' test: would the audience cheer? If yes, double the Force Point. PACING: Star Wars stories follow a pattern — start in media res (action already happening), escalate through complications, hit a low point (the heroes are captured or outmatched), then build to a climactic finish where the heroes triumph. IMPROVISING: Players will go off-script. Embrace it. The D6 system is flexible enough to handle anything. When in doubt, set a difficulty, let them roll, and narrate the result cinematically.

chunks.title: Common Situations & Rules
chunks.text: CHASES: Opposed piloting/driving rolls. The leader sets the pace; the pursuer must match or exceed. Terrain and obstacles add difficulty. Ramming is an opposed roll — the rammer deals Body damage to the target, and the target deals Body damage to the rammer. SNEAKING: Sneak skill vs the target's Search or Perception. Modifiers: darkness gives +1D to Sneak, noise gives -1D, moving slowly gives +1D. SOCIAL ENCOUNTERS: Con vs target's Willpower or Perception to deceive. Bargain vs Bargain for negotiations. Persuasion vs Willpower to convince. Command vs Willpower to order (requires authority). SLICING COMPUTERS: Computer Programming/Repair vs the system's security difficulty. More secure systems = higher difficulty. Military systems are typically Difficult to Heroic. PICKING LOCKS: Security skill vs the lock's difficulty. Simple lock = Easy, Standard = Moderate, High Security = Difficult, Military = Very Difficult, Imperial Palace = Heroic. FALLING: 1D damage per 3 meters fallen. Climbing/Jumping or Dexterity roll can reduce fall damage. DROWNING/SUFFOCATION: Stamina roll each round, increasing difficulty. Failure = stunned, multiple failures = incapacitated, then mortally wounded. ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS: Extreme heat/cold, vacuum, radiation — all require Stamina rolls at GM-set difficulties with escalating penalties. CALLED SHOTS: +1D difficulty for torso, +2D for limbs, +3D for hands/head, +4D or more for specific small targets (weapon, belt, control panel).
